subject.title: [Feature]: Global agent killswitch (pause/abort) triggerable via Signal and CLI

question: Should cooperative gateway suspension become a persistent operator-controlled safety state that can abort active work, and which authenticated principals and surfaces may engage and clear it?
rationale: Source inspection establishes the missing capability but cannot choose the intended denial-of-service boundary, recovery contract, persistence behavior, or whether remote channel control should ship with the first version.

options.title: Extend canonical suspension
options.body: Evolve the existing gateway admission coordinator into the single persistent safety state, with authenticated RPC/CLI control and a generic channel invocation seam.

options.title: Ship local control first
options.body: Add aborting persistent RPC/CLI control while deferring Signal engagement and revival until its identity and replay model is separately approved.

options.title: Keep suspension host-only
options.body: Retain the current short refuse-only host lease and continue using gateway service stop for emergency containment.

recommendation.title: Extend canonical suspension
recommendation.body: Evolve the existing gateway admission coordinator into the single persistent safety state, with authenticated RPC/CLI control and a generic channel invocation seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent cooperative suspension implementation is the closest canonical owner boundary, and its author is best positioned to decide whether it should expand into operator-visible safety state.
